newsitem.title: FRANCE: French hero of Britain's RAF dies.
newsitem.headline: French hero of Britain's RAF dies.

text.p: Retired air force General Yves Ezanno, one of the first French pilots to escape from occupied Europe during World War Two to fight with Britain's Royal Air Force, has died aged 84, his family said on Wednesday.

Ezanno, then a lieutenant, illegally took a light aircraft to Britain in the summer of 1940, answering the call to arms and French resistance issued from London on June 18 that year by General Charles de Gaulle.
Assigned to a Free French light bomber squadron in the RAF, Ezanno first saw action over Libya, Egypt and the Mediterranean against German Marshal Erwin Rommel's Afrika Korps.
Ezzano was later assigned to the RAF itself. He commanded its 198 Fighter Squadron flying Typhoons on low-level ground attack missions.
He flew over Normandy during the D-Day invasion in 1944. He was shot down and wounded over the Netherlands later that year.
After the war, Ezzano rose in the French air force, leaving in 1967 as head of its fighter command after occupying several top NATO posts.
He was awarded the British and American Distinguished Flying Crosses, both with bars.
